$comment: Everything a church spends money on, for the United Under God buying program. Category, then subcategories, then typical items. No prices or vendor names: prices come only from awarded bids in the buying book.

categories.name: Office supplies and paper
categories.short: Copy paper, pens, folders, labels, and the everyday desk supplies every church office runs on.
categories.summary: Every church office goes through the same paper, pens, folders, and labels. These are stocked items with a unit price, so they suit a standing group catalog that any church can order from when it needs to.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church office supplies: copy paper, cardstock, pens, folders, labels, and binders, priced from bids churches can order from as needed.

items.name: Copy paper, letter size, 20 lb
specs: Sheets per ream and reams per case

categories.name: Printing, copiers, and signage
categories.short: Toner, copier leases, bulletins, offering envelopes, and signs.
categories.summary: Toner and copiers are where many churches overpay first. Toner is a stocked item with a unit price; copier leases and service are recurring contracts; printed pieces and signs are quoted jobs.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church printing: toner, copier leases and service, bulletins, offering envelopes, and signage, from bids churches can buy from.

subcategories.name: Toner and ink
specs: Printer and copier makes and models

items.name: Copier lease
specs: Pages per month, black and color

items.name: Copier service and supplies agreement
specs: Cost per page, black and color

items.name: Printer monitoring and automatic toner reorder

categories.name: Postage and mailing
categories.short: Postage meters, bulk mail, mailers, and shipping.
categories.summary: Newsletters, giving statements, and appeal letters all go through the mail. Meters and shipping accounts are recurring contracts; mailing jobs are quoted per piece.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church postage and mailing: postage meter leases, bulk mail services, mailers, and shipping rates, from bids.

items.name: Mailing house for newsletters and appeals
Address list cleanup before a mailing

categories.name: Communion and baptism
categories.short: Communion cups, bread, juice, trays, and baptism robes and towels.
categories.summary: Communion supplies are bought on a steady rhythm by nearly every church, which makes them a natural group catalog. Baptism supplies are smaller, steady purchases.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for communion and baptism supplies: prefilled cups, wafers, juice, trays, baptism robes, and towels, from bids.

categories.name: Worship, choir, and music
categories.short: Music licenses, hymnals, choir robes, sheet music, and piano tuning.
categories.summary: Worship carries steady costs: the licenses to sing and stream songs, hymnals and choir music, robes, and keeping instruments in tune.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church worship and music: copyright and streaming licenses, hymnals, choir robes, sheet music, and piano and organ service.

items.name: Performance license for concerts and events

categories.name: Children's and youth ministry
categories.short: Curriculum, VBS, camp, crafts, snacks, and check-in supplies.
categories.summary: Children's and youth ministry buys the same things on the same calendar: curriculum each quarter, VBS each summer, camp, crafts, and snacks every week.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for children's and youth ministry: Sunday school curriculum, VBS kits, camp, craft supplies, snacks, and check-in labels, from bids.

categories.name: Bibles and Bible study
categories.short: Pew and outreach Bibles, study books, and devotionals.
categories.summary: Bibles for the pews, Bibles to give away, and study books for every small group are steady purchases that add up across a congregation.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for Bibles and Bible study: pew Bibles, outreach Bibles, children's Bibles, small group study books, and devotionals.

categories.name: Kitchen and fellowship
categories.short: Plates, cups, coffee, food for meals, kitchen equipment, and hood cleaning.
categories.summary: Wednesday suppers, funerals, and fellowship meals run on paper goods, coffee, and a working kitchen. Supplies suit a catalog; equipment is quoted; hood cleaning and repair are service contracts.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church kitchens and fellowship halls: paper goods, coffee, food for meals, kitchen appliances, and hood and grease trap service.

items.name: Hot and cold cups with lids
Foil, film, and food storage bags

categories.name: Janitorial and restroom supplies
categories.short: Toilet tissue, paper towels, soap, cleaners, trash liners, and mats.
categories.summary: Restroom paper, soap, cleaners, and trash liners are bought by the case every month. They are the easiest group catalog to set up and to order from.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church janitorial and restroom supplies: toilet tissue, paper towels, hand soap, cleaners, can liners, and entrance mats.

categories.name: Janitorial service
categories.short: Weekly cleaning, carpet cleaning, floor care, and windows.
categories.summary: Many churches clean with volunteers until they cannot. A janitorial contract is a recurring service bid by region, so churches in the same area can be bid together.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church janitorial service: weekly cleaning, after-event cleaning, carpet cleaning, floor stripping and waxing, and window washing.

subcategories.name: Cleaning service
specs: Proof of insurance and background checks

categories.name: Facilities maintenance
categories.short: HVAC service, plumbing, electrical, roofing, painting, flooring, pews, and elevators.
categories.summary: Buildings are a church's largest asset and often its largest surprise expense. Routine service suits a regional contract; repairs and replacements are quoted projects.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church facilities maintenance: HVAC service, plumbing, electrical, roofing, painting, flooring, pew refinishing, and elevator service.

items.name: Stained glass repair and protective glazing

categories.name: Grounds and parking
categories.short: Lawn care, landscaping, snow removal, parking lot sealing and striping, and tree service.
categories.summary: Grounds care is the first impression of a church and a recurring bill. Lawn care and snow removal are seasonal contracts bid by region; paving and tree work are quoted projects.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church grounds: lawn care, landscaping, mulch, snow removal, parking lot sealing and striping, asphalt repair, and tree service.

categories.name: Pest control
categories.short: General pest service, termite protection, rodents, and wildlife.
categories.summary: Pest service is a recurring contract nearly every church carries. It bids well by region, since providers already route trucks through the same neighborhoods.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church pest control: general pest service, termite protection, rodent control, mosquito service, and wildlife removal.

items.name: Bed bug treatment for shelters and guest rooms

categories.name: Security and life safety
categories.short: Cameras, access control, alarm monitoring, fire inspections, first aid and AEDs, and volunteer background checks.
categories.summary: Keeping people safe has recurring costs: alarm monitoring, required fire inspections, AED supplies, and background checks for anyone who works with children.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church security and safety: cameras, access control, alarm monitoring, fire extinguisher and sprinkler inspection, AEDs, and background checks.

requires.note: Background checks need each person's written consent and follow federal and state consumer-report rules. The screening company handles the consent and the report.

items.name: Background checks for staff and volunteers

categories.name: Utilities and telecom
categories.short: Electric and gas supply, water, waste and recycling, internet, phones, and mobile lines.
categories.summary: Utilities are paid every month whether anyone notices or not. Some can be bid, such as waste hauling, internet, and phones; energy supply can be bid only where the state lets customers choose a supplier.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church utilities: electric and natural gas supply where choice is allowed, waste and recycling, internet, phone service, and mobile lines.

requires.note: Electric and gas supply can be bid only where the state allows customers to choose a supplier. Elsewhere the local utility sets the rate.

categories.name: Energy savings
categories.short: LED lighting retrofits, energy audits, smart thermostats, and solar where offered.
categories.summary: Lowering what a building uses is the other half of the utility bill. Retrofits and solar are quoted projects; rebates and incentives depend on where the church is.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church energy savings: LED lighting retrofits, energy audits, smart thermostats, lighting controls, and solar where offered.

requires.note: Solar is offered only where providers serve the area, and incentives for nonprofits vary by state and utility.

categories.name: Technology
categories.short: Computers, software subscriptions, church management, website, email, IT support, cybersecurity, and backup.
categories.summary: A church office runs on a few computers and a handful of subscriptions. Hardware suits a catalog; IT support, security, and backup are recurring contracts.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church technology: computers, software subscriptions, church management software, websites, email, IT support, cybersecurity, and data backup.

categories.name: Sound, livestream, and lighting
categories.short: Sound, livestream, lighting, projectors and screens, video, and hearing assistance.
categories.summary: Sound, livestream, and lighting are planned for each sanctuary and installed as projects, with your volunteers trained.
categories.metaDescription: Church sound, livestream, lighting, projectors, video, and hearing assistance, planned for your sanctuary.

categories.name: Transportation
categories.short: Church vans and buses, fuel, maintenance, tires, and charter trips.
categories.summary: A church van or bus carries youth trips, senior outings, and Sunday pickups. Vehicles are quoted purchases; fuel and maintenance are contracts; vehicle insurance goes through a licensed agent.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church transportation: vans and buses, fleet fuel, vehicle maintenance, tires, charter buses, and driver checks.

requires.note: Referral only, through a licensed insurance agent or broker. United Under God does not sell insurance, quote it, or advise on coverage. A licensed professional reviews your church and recommends coverage.

categories.name: Insurance
categories.short: Property, liability, abuse and molestation, directors and officers, and workers' compensation.
categories.summary: Insurance is one of a church's largest fixed costs, and it is handled only by licensed professionals. We introduce churches to licensed agents and brokers who serve churches; we do not sell or quote coverage.
categories.metaDescription: Church insurance by introduction to a licensed agent or broker: property, general liability, abuse and molestation, directors and officers, and workers' compensation.

requires.note: Referral only, through a licensed insurance agent or broker. United Under God does not sell insurance, quote it, or advise on coverage. A licensed professional reviews your church and recommends coverage.

categories.name: Financial services
categories.short: Bookkeeping, online giving and card processing, payroll, audit and tax, and banking.
categories.summary: Money handling is where trust matters most. Bookkeeping and giving tools can be bid. Payroll and tax, audits, and banking and loans are by introduction to a licensed or qualified provider only.
categories.metaDescription: Church financial services: bookkeeping, online giving and card processing, and introductions to qualified payroll, audit, tax, and banking providers.

items.name: Online giving platform
specs: Fees passed to giver or not

requires.note: Referral only, through a qualified payroll provider or tax professional such as a CPA or enrolled agent. United Under God does not process payroll or give tax advice.
Referral only, through a licensed CPA firm. United Under God does not perform audits or prepare tax filings.
Referral only, to a licensed lender or chartered bank or credit union. United Under God does not lend money, arrange loans, or advise on banking.

categories.name: Staff, HR, and benefits
categories.short: Health insurance, retirement plans, office help, nursery workers, and HR support.
categories.summary: Staff are a church's largest expense. Health and retirement benefits go through licensed professionals only; office help, nursery staffing, and HR support can be bid.
categories.metaDescription: Church staffing and benefits: introductions to licensed health and retirement benefit providers, plus office help, nursery staffing, and HR support.

requires.note: Referral only, through a licensed benefits agent or broker. United Under God does not sell insurance or advise on benefits.
Referral only, through a licensed financial professional or plan provider. United Under God does not offer or advise on retirement plans.

categories.name: Professional services
categories.short: Architecture and engineering, appraisals, and consulting.
categories.summary: Churches need professionals now and then: an architect for a building, an appraiser for a sale, a consultant for a campaign.
categories.metaDescription: Professional services for churches: architecture, engineering, appraisals, and campaign and planning consultants, bid for the group.

requires.note: Architecture and engineering are performed by licensed professionals. Bids compare licensed firms.

categories.name: Events and promotion
categories.short: Tents, rentals, T-shirts, banners, promotional items, and event supplies.
categories.summary: Fall festivals, revivals, and homecomings bring rental and printing costs. Shirts and printed items suit a catalog; rentals are quoted per event.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church events: tent and table rentals, portable restrooms, T-shirts, banners, yard signs, and promotional items.

categories.name: Outreach and missions
categories.short: Benevolence supplies, food pantry stock, hygiene kits, and mission trip costs.
categories.summary: Outreach budgets stretch furthest when supplies are bought together: pantry stock by the case, hygiene kit items in bulk, and coats and socks before winter.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church outreach and missions: food pantry stock, hygiene kit supplies, blankets, socks, school supplies, and mission trip lodging.

items.name: Rice, pasta, cereal, and dry goods

categories.name: Cemetery care
categories.short: Cemetery mowing, grave opening and closing, monument repair, and records.
categories.summary: Churches with a cemetery carry a second set of grounds costs. Mowing and grave services are contracts; monument repair and mapping are quoted projects.
categories.metaDescription: Group bids for church cemetery care: cemetery mowing, grave opening and closing, monument cleaning and repair, fencing, and plot mapping.

categories.name: Furniture
categories.short: Chairs, tables, office and classroom furniture, and storage.
categories.summary: Stacking chairs, folding tables, classroom sets, and office desks are bought in quantity and replaced on a cycle, which suits a group catalog.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church furniture: stacking chairs, folding tables, classroom furniture, office desks and chairs, chancel furniture, and storage.

categories.name: Nursery
categories.short: Cribs, changing tables, toys, diapers and wipes, and safety supplies.
categories.summary: A clean, safe nursery tells young families they are expected. Equipment is replaced on a cycle; diapers, wipes, and sanitizer are monthly supplies.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church nurseries: cribs, changing tables, high chairs, toys, diapers and wipes, sanitizer, and safety gates.

categories.name: Flowers, candles, and decor
categories.short: Altar flowers, candles, paraments, and sanctuary decor.
categories.summary: Altar flowers each week and candles for every service are steady, quiet costs. A standing flower order is a contract; candles and paraments suit a catalog.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for church flowers and decor: weekly altar flowers, memorial arrangements, altar candles, paraments, and sanctuary decor.

categories.name: Christmas, Easter, and the church year
categories.short: Poinsettias, Christmas candles, Easter lilies, egg hunts, and Advent and Palm Sunday supplies.
categories.summary: The church year brings the same purchases every season. Ordering them together, early, is exactly what a group bid is for.
categories.metaDescription: Group buying for Christmas, Easter, and the church year: poinsettias, candlelight service candles, Easter lilies, egg hunt supplies, palms, and Advent candles.

items.name: Candlelight service candles with drip guards
